input.content: Pattern: removing an ownership guard during a "simplification". In cleanup.py, cleanup_setup(store, workspace_id, setup_id) used compare-and-delete on store.active[workspace_id] (pop only if association["setup_id"] == setup_id). The guard was replaced by an unconditional pop. Result: cancelling a pending re-setup, or cleaning up a superseded setup, deletes the workspace's current active connection that belongs to another setup. Rule: when a dict is keyed by a shared key (workspace) but the cleanup is scoped to a narrower identity (setup_id), keep the identity check. Existing tests only covered the "cleanup own association" path, so they pass with or without the guard — require a test for the "different setup owns the association" case.
